content_metadata.description: An educational video demonstrating the Wiimote's Bluetooth features and exploring how it can be used beyond gaming, focusing on its ability to measure acceleration and motion.

qAndA.question: What color line represents the vertical measurement on the graph?

qAndA.answer: The red, blue, and green lines briefly converge, indicating equal acceleration values.
qAndA.question: What happens to the acceleration values when the Wiimote is dropped?

qAndA.answer: It's due to the constant downward force of gravity.
qAndA.question: Why does the vertical measurement (red line) show a higher value when the Wiimote is resting on the table?
What technology does the Wiimote use to connect to a computer?

qAndA.answer: Using it as a pointing device for a computer screen, similar to a mouse.
qAndA.question: What future application for the Wiimote does the speaker mention?

activities.description: Demonstrating a graph on a computer screen displaying acceleration values from the Wiimote.
Rotating and tilting the Wiimote to show changes in the graph's values.
Continuously manipulating the Wiimote to generate different acceleration values on the graph.

Dropping the Wiimote and observing how acceleration values briefly become equal in freefall.
Summarizing the demonstration and future possibilities of using the Wiimote as a pointing device.

youtube_description:
We are working on documenting and adding support for the Wiimote on Bluetooth-enabled computers. Here's how it's turning out so far. Stay tuned for pointing, Mii data (already working!), and much, much more!

See this for more info: http://www.wiili.org/Wiimote
